Therefore, the path of light is for the satisfaction of the senses of God. But those who are
disoriented or ignorant, they, Arjuna and others, while following the path shown by the devotees,
without making any effort to satisfy the divine senses of God, follow the path of self-realization.
They follow.
In contrast, they make artificial efforts to stop the functions of the senses (Yoga
Method) or disregard the divine senses of God (FFE). But devotees are above the yogis
and the wise, Because they do not deny the senses of God; they want to satisfy the senses of God. Only the wise and yogis, due to their ignorance, deny the senses of God
and artificially want to gain control over the functions of their diseased senses. When the senses become diseased, their attachment to material needs increases.
When a person sees the harms of increasing the functions of the senses, then he is called a wise man.
And when a person wants to stop the functions of those same senses through the practice of the rules of Yoga,
then he is called a Yogi, but when the same person becomes fully aware of God with divine senses
and wants to satisfy those senses, then he is called a devotee of God.   A devotee of God
never denies the senses of God, Nor do they artificially stop the functions of the senses.
But they voluntarily engage their sacred senses in the service of the master of the senses, as Arjuna did.
And in this way, they attain perfection in satisfying God, which is the ultimate of all accomplishments
